claims.text: A novel eutectic-alloy design strategy can produce alternating soft FCC and hard BCC phases in a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The resulting soft-FCC/hard-BCC phase architecture constitutes a hierarchical microstructure.
Combining soft FCC and hard BCC phases through microstructure design causes strength and ductility to increase simultaneously relative to conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The intervention will increase strength by 20% relative to conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The intervention will increase ductility by 15% relative to conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The simultaneous strength and ductility benefit should persist at operating temperatures up to 700°C.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility increases depends on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions.
An increase of at least 10% in both strength and ductility is defined as a significant result in the proposed falsification test.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20% higher strength and 15% higher ductility, whereas the falsification rule treats 10% increases in each as significant. Thus, results between these thresholds could pass the stated test while failing to meet the stated prediction.
